quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is crossing the street, what should you do?

options.text: You must always yield the right-of-way.
You must tell them where to cross the street.
You only have to yield the right-of-way if you are at a corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind pedestrians use a white cane or guide dog. You must always yield the right-of-way to these pedestrians.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.
You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. You may turn once the intersection is clear and the signal allows.

questions.question: When must you stop your vehicle?

options.text: At any intersection where a police officer orders you to stop.
Where there is a red traffic light.

questions.explanation: Stop at a red traffic light. Always obey traffic officers, even if their instructions differ from signs or signals.

questions.question: When can you pass a vehicle?

options.text: When you are on a hill or curve.
When you are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.
When you are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you can pass. A solid line means you cannot pass. Only pass when it is safe.

questions.question: If a green traffic light is showing and a police officer signals you to stop, what should you do?

options.text: Do what the vehicle in front of you does.

questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer, even if their orders contradict traffic signals or signs.

questions.question: How can drowsiness affect your driving?
questions.explanation: Drowsiness impairs judgment, slows reaction time, and decreases awareness—just like alcohol and drugs.

questions.question: Which statement is true about railroad crossings?

options.text: You should use cruise control near a railroad crossing to maintain a constant speed.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal. Be careful near railroad tracks.

questions.question: South Dakota law requires ____ to wear safety belts in a moving vehicle.

options.text: Drivers, front seat passengers, and children

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers, front seat passengers, and children
questions.explanation: Drivers, front seat passengers, and children under 18 must wear safety belts. Young children should sit in the back seat.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: Speed up so you can make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal to turn from the indicated lane.
Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow is ending. Prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic pass before turning.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.explanation: Only time reduces BAC. Nothing else—including food and caffeine—speeds up this process.

questions.question: If you become tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Stop to rest or change drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or change drivers.
questions.explanation: If you become tired while driving, stop to rest or change drivers. Tiredness makes you less alert and slows your reactions, which is dangerous.

questions.question: What is this bicyclist signaling?
questions.explanation: Bicycles don't have turn signals. Bicyclists use hand and arm signals instead. When a bicyclist puts their left arm straight out, they are signaling a left turn.

questions.question: Alcohol and/or drugs affect which driving skills?
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs harm many driving skills. They slow your reaction time, hurt your coordination, reduce alertness, and make it hard to concentrate.

questions.question: Who can use handicap parking spaces?

options.text: Anyone, but only if all other spaces are full.
Only drivers with the correct license plate or hanging tag.
People who are not feeling well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only drivers with the correct license plate or hanging tag.
questions.explanation: Handicap parking spaces are for people with disabilities. To park in one, you must have the right license plate or hanging tag with the international symbol.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that an intersection is ahead so you can slow down and be ready to turn or deal with traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a yield sign is coming up. Start to slow down when you see this warning.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC) and alcohol's effects.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body and reduces its harmful effects.

questions.question: As daylight fades, you should turn on your:
questions.explanation: As it gets dark, use your low beam headlights so others can see you. Use high beams only when no other drivers are around.

questions.question: Before entering an intersection, look to your:
questions.explanation: Before entering an intersection, check both left and right for cars or pedestrians. Look left a second time because cars from your left will be closer. Look all the way across the intersection to make sure it is clear.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop if cars are approaching.
Come to a full stop, then proceed when safe.
Proceed carefully through the intersection without always stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop, then proceed when safe.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means stop. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line. If there is no line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop at a point where you can see oncoming traffic. Only move when it is safe.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Make drivers angry about slow traffic.
Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for workers and drivers. Watch for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests. These warn you and show you where to go.

questions.question: It is unlawful to:

options.text: Pass another vehicle in any marked no passing zone.
Pass another vehicle over a railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills, curves, or where you cannot see far ahead. You cannot pass at street crossings, railroad crossings, in no passing zones, or where a solid yellow line is next to your lane. Do not pass when the car in front has stopped for a pedestrian or in work zones.

questions.question: When should drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if the pedestrians first wave to the driver.
Only if the pedestrians are not texting while walking.

questions.explanation: Stop completely at a crosswalk for any pedestrian. Only move forward when your lane is fully clear.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a steep hill coming up. Slow down and be ready to brake to avoid crashes and brake damage.

questions.question: Before returning to your original lane after passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When passing, watch for both headlights of the car you passed in your rearview mirror. Only then is it safe to move back to your original lane.
